what_its_for: Methocarbamol is a muscle relaxer used to treat pain and discomfort caused by muscle spasms, strains, and sprains. It works on your central nervous system (brain and spinal cord) to help your muscles relax. It is usually used together with rest and physical therapy.
how_to_take: Take methocarbamol exactly as your doctor tells you. You can take it with or without food. If it upsets your stomach, try taking it with food or milk. Swallow the tablet whole with a full glass of water. Do not crush or chew the tablet unless your doctor says it is okay. Take it at the same times each day to help you remember.
dosing: The usual adult starting dose is 1,500 mg (three 500 mg tablets) taken 4 times a day for the first 2 to 3 days. After that, your doctor may lower your dose to 750 mg taken every 4 hours, or 1,500 mg taken 3 times a day. Do not take more than 8,000 mg per day. Your doctor will adjust your dose based on your condition. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not double up or take two doses at the same time to make up for the one you missed.
storage: Store methocarbamol tablets at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C and 25°C). Keep the tablets away from heat, direct sunlight, and moisture. Do not store them in the bathroom. Keep this medication in its original container with the lid tightly closed. Keep all medications out of reach of children and pets. Ask your pharmacist how to safely dispose of any unused medication.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol while taking methocarbamol. Alcohol can make drowsiness and dizziness much worse and can be dangerous. Do not drive a car, operate heavy machinery, or do any activity that requires you to be alert until you know how this medication affects you, because it can cause drowsiness and slow your reaction time. Avoid taking other medications that cause drowsiness such as sleeping pills, anxiety medications, other muscle relaxers, narcotic pain medicines, or allergy medications without first talking to your doctor or pharmacist.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor right away if you experience any of the following: a severe allergic reaction such as rash, itching, hives, swelling of your face, lips, tongue, or throat, or trouble breathing; yellowing of your skin or eyes (signs of liver problems); dark or brown colored urine; feeling faint or fainting; a slow or irregular heartbeat; seizures; memory loss or confusion; or if your muscle pain or spasms do not improve or get worse after a few days of treatment.
when_it_works: Methocarbamol usually starts working within 30 minutes to 1 hour after you take it. Most people begin to feel relief from muscle spasms and pain within the first few days of treatment. It works best when used along with rest and physical therapy as directed by your doctor.
special_populations: Older adults (65 years and older) may be more sensitive to the drowsiness and dizziness this medication causes, which can increase the risk of falls. Use with caution and talk to your doctor about the right dose. This medication is generally not recommended for children under 16 years of age. If you are pregnant or breastfeeding, talk to your doctor before taking methocarbamol, as it is not known if it is safe during pregnancy or nursing. People with kidney disease should use this medication with caution. This medication should be avoided in patients with known seizure disorders.
